summary: The WebApp has 150 client route entries (25 page routes, a 404 fallback and 124 redirects), about 146 screen states, 20 kinds of email, 176 API routes, 14 timers or crons, 21 external services, 249 env names and 78 Firestore collections. Thirty-five API routes have no caller, about 9,000 lines in 36 files never run from any entry point, and the dropped early trial still accounts for about 10,500 lines across five mounted routers, a worker loop and the site job page's phases. The deploy config misdescribes the worker, which actually runs the auto-send and outcome-question loops, and three site-intake browser suites never run in CI. Production counts show no company send and no introduction yet, and no screen shows the owner those totals.

findings.today: The server answers 35 routes that nothing calls: the robot-team registry and supply agreements (6), the owned Atlas reconstruction routes (5, which can start paid compute), two trial progress routes, the site measurements and item routes, the job-workflow owner routes, run-closure, advisory-retry, operator-status and others. findings.should: Every route the server answers has a caller and a reason.
findings.proposal: One PR per router: delete the 35 handlers listed in inventory-webapp.md section 3a with their now-unused helpers and tests, and drop the stale /api/job-workflow/owner mock from site-private-link-reliability.spec.ts. findings.user_result: No customer-visible change; less code that can break or be abused, and faster reviews.
findings.risk: An operator or Pipeline release older than HEAD may still call a route (the Pipeline's active release can lag HEAD). Request logs settle it. The owned Atlas routes could start paid work if someone found them, which is a reason to remove them, not to keep them.

findings.title: The dropped early trial still lives in about 10,500 lines, five mounted routers, a worker and the site's job-page states
evidence: webapp:server/routes.ts:71-73,88,130-137 mount internal-beta-policy-screening, internal-scene-execution-window, internal-owner-success-proposal, internal-task-evaluation-launches, -submissions, -preparations
webapp:server/worker.ts:46 starts the Task Evaluation launch forwarder
webapp:client/src/lib/jobOutlook.ts:5-13 phases testing and result, reasons run_held, run_ended, no_ai_robot_scored, window_ended_during_test
webapp:client/src/lib/jobOutlook.ts:70-74 'a trial result'
webapp:server/utils/policyIntegration.ts:123 hard-codes a robot-policy endpoint https://api.dreamlabs.ai/v1/get_action, imported by robotTeamSupply.ts
webapp:client/src/app/routes.tsx LegacyBookExactSiteReviewRedirect adds interest=task-evaluation-run
measured: 34 source files / 10,514 lines and 16 test files / 6,426 lines named for the trial (report section 10)
baseline aggregate: taskEvaluationLaunches 524 docs, taskEvaluationPolicyRuns 121, captureTaskEvaluationRuns 95
findings.today: The trial was dropped on 2026-11-14 and the doctrine says Blueprint runs no robot software in the simulation. The WebApp still mounts its routers, runs its forwarder, keeps 'testing' and 'result' phases in the site's job-page model and keeps a robot-policy integration. Part of this code is now the job's launch path to the Pipeline under the trial's old names (#1300), so the line between live and dead is hard to see.
findings.should: Only the job-launch path survives, under job words; trial routes, phases, reasons and the policy integration are gone.
findings.proposal: Step 1 (S): remove phases testing/result and reasons run_held/run_ended/no_ai_robot_scored/window_ended_during_test from jobOutlook.ts and the server outlook, after checking no live job holds them (Firestore aggregate 3). Step 2 (M): delete policyIntegration.ts, policyCanary*.ts, runResultScoring.ts, evaluationReadyRunContract.ts, robotTeamTestSubmission.ts and the two uncalled trial routes. Step 3 (M): rename the surviving launch path from taskEvaluation* to job launch.
findings.user_result: The site's job page can never show a trial state; one fewer concept for anyone reading the code.
findings.risk: The launch forwarder and launch contracts carry today's job to the Pipeline. Deleting by name instead of by caller would stop new jobs. Do it caller-first, with the core-journey test green.
findings.requirement_source: owner direction 2026-11-14 (trial dropped); doctrine line 'no robot software in the simulation' (#1322, 2026-11-19)

findings.title: The deploy config says the worker only forwards launches, but the worker runs all seven job loops
evidence: webapp:render.yaml:31-33 'explicitly constrained to Task Evaluation launch reconciliation; unrelated ops processors stay off'
webapp:render.yaml:53 BLUEPRINT_TASK_EVALUATION_LAUNCH_FORWARD_ONLY_WORKER=true
webapp:render.required.env.example:18 'must not enable unrelated ops automation'
webapp:server/worker.ts:22-27,36-44 the flag only changes a log line
webapp:server/worker.ts:46-58 starts launch forwarder, withdrawals, deletions, job window sweep, automatic sends, outcome questions and heartbeat unconditionally
findings.today: Anyone reading render.yaml or the env manifest believes the worker does one thing. It actually sends every job to the approved companies, asks the 14/45/90-day outcome questions, ends expired jobs and deletes withdrawn videos. The flag that claims to restrict it does nothing.
findings.should: The config and its comments say what the worker does; no flag pretends to limit it.
findings.proposal: Delete BLUEPRINT_TASK_EVALUATION_LAUNCH_FORWARD_ONLY_WORKER from worker.ts, render.yaml and render.required.env.example, and rewrite the two comments to list the seven loops.
findings.user_result: An operator cannot 'fix' the worker to match the comment and silently stop job sends and outcome emails.
findings.risk: None in code; the flag has no effect today.
findings.requirement_source: nobody: the flag outlived the change that gave the worker its job loops

findings.title: Storage rules still let any signed-in account upload to folders of retired products
evidence: webapp:storage.rules:116-142 users/, accounts/, captures/, capture-artifacts/ writable by any signed-in user for their own uid (500 MB per object for captures and capture-artifacts)
webapp:storage.rules:107 blueprints/ (100 MB)
webapp:storage.rules:177-190 menus/ any signed-in user, 10 MB, no count limit
webapp:storage.rules:145-160 scenes raw path, 20 GiB per object, kept for the Android capture app
cmd: grep -rn 'firebase/storage|uploadBytes' client/src -> only getStorage import in client/src/lib/firebase.ts:27; no client upload
webapp:server/utils/storage-provider.ts:213-218 the only code naming blueprints/, menus/, capture-artifacts/
findings.today: The website never uploads to Storage from the browser, yet the rules allow any signed-in Firebase account to store files under menus/, blueprints/, users/, accounts/, captures/ and capture-artifacts/, and the retired capture app's raw path takes 20 GiB objects. Blueprint pays for whatever is stored.
findings.should: Only paths the current product writes are client-writable; the rest deny by default.
findings.proposal: Remove the menus/, blueprints/, users/, accounts/ and capture-artifacts/ rules, and drop the client create rule on scenes/**/raw once the Capture repo confirms the Android app is retired; the deny-all at storage.rules:193 then covers them. Coordinate with the Capture repo, which deploys the same rules file.
findings.user_result: No customer-visible change; closes a storage-cost and abuse surface.
findings.risk: The rules are shared with the Capture repo and deploys are last-writer-wins (storage.rules:144); both repos must change together. Existing objects stay; only new client writes stop.
findings.requirement_source: nobody found for menus/, blueprints/, users/, accounts/; capture app (retired 2026-11-11) for the raw path

findings.risk: Count queries cost Firestore reads; aggregate count() queries keep that small.

findings.user_result: The policy says exactly where a site's data goes.
findings.risk: Listing a processor not used is safer than omitting one used; only remove it after the owner confirms.
